newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SKorea defence ministry to inspect airports.
newsitem.headline: SKorea defence ministry to inspect airports.

text.p: South Korea's Ministry of National Defence said on Tuesday it would start inspecting 12 airports around the country next week to ensure flight safety after the fatal crash of a Korean Air Lines (KAL) plane in Guam.
"We maintain the airport facilities on a regular basis but have decided to conduct an overall check after the accident of KAL," said an official at the defence ministry.
The official who declined to be identified said South Korea has 16 airports of which four are under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Construction and Transportation.

The transportation ministry said it started its own inspection of the four airports on Tuesday, including Kimpo Airport in Seoul and an airport on the southern island of Cheju, a popular holiday destination.
A statement by the defence ministry said it would seek the cooperation of the transportation ministry and an air force specialist on air-traffic control for next week's examinations.

An investigation is under way by the U.S. National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) to determine why KAL's Boeing 747 carrying 254 people ploughed into a hill minutes before landing at the airport on the Pacific island.
So far 28 people have survived the tragedy. Twenty-two survivors were airlifted back to Seoul for treatment. Most of them suffer burns and cuts, but doctors say their lives are not in danger.
A mother and her daughter, both Americans of Korean descent suffering bruises but no burns, arrived in Seoul on Tuesday.
KAL officials have said an out-of-service landing instrument is one possible cause of the accident. The KAL officials also acknowledge they had known about repairs on the instrument.

The defence ministry said it would be looking over control tower facilities and instruments and procedures used in the landing and take off of planes. It would also inspect airports' emergency plans to deal with accidents.
